lawyer:
Subrata Chowdhury, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
QA Hossain, AAG ----- For the Respondent No. 1. 
SS Halder with Shahed Alam, Advocates ----- For the Respondent No. 5.
parties:
Nilkhi Arial Kha Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. represented by its President Md. Alimuzzaman Khalashi ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
The Secretary, Ministry of Land and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammad Habibur Rahman, J.: This Rule Nisi was issued on 25th November, 1990 calling upon the respondent No. 1. Secretary, Ministry of Land, No. 2, Member-1, Land Appeal Board, Dhaka, No. 3, Additional Commissioner, Dhaka Division, Dhaka, No. 4 Additional Deputy Commissioner. (Revenue), Madaripur and No. 5, Nikhil Chandra Malo, Secretary, Kabirajpur Union Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. of Kabirajpur, Upazila Bajar, District Madaripur to show cause why the order Annexure 'H' dated 4.11.90 passed by Mr. AZM Nasiruddin, Secretary, Ministry of Land under Memo No. Bhu; Ma: Sha-9-26/90/1147/(2) appeal and the order dated 22.11.89 Annexure 'F'; passed by respondent No: 3; Additional Commissioner; Dhaka Division, Dhaka cancelling the three years' lease from 1396 BS to 1398 BS of Shiruail to Nilkhi Baddha Jalmahal- (closed fishery), Upazila Shibchar District Madaripur dated 31.1.89 executed by respondent No. 4 Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur in favour of the petitioner should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. 

 2. The case of the petitioner Nilkhi Arial Kha Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. represented by its President Md. Alimuzzaman is, that it is a registered co-operative society having registrative No. 1527 dated 21.8.72 under the Co-operative Society Act, 1940 consisting of 43 members who are all fishermen earning their livelihood from fishing. The petitioner society being the previous lessee of Shiruail to Nilkhi Jalmahal measuring 470 acres ( a closed fishery) for the years 1394 BS to 1395 BS applied to the respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur on 2.1.89 for settlement of the said closed fishery for a term of three years from 1396 BS to 1398 BS at 25% enhanced rate which was duly recommended by the District Co-operative Officer. The respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur sent his Memo No. 63 SA dated 15.1.89 (Annexure A) to the petitioner stating as follows : 

 Thereafter, respondent No.4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Madaripur wrote his memo Annexure A(1) dated 21.1.89 to the petitioner stating as follows: 

 In pursuance of the aforesaid order Annexure A (1) dated 21.1.89 the petitioner Society on 13.2.89 deposited Tk. 18,750.00 as rent for the said Jalmahal for the year 1396 BS by annexure B (Duplicate Carbon Receipt) dated 13.2.89 at 25% higher rent than the previous year's lease money. Thereafter on 21.3.89 the lease deed Annexure 'C' was executed between the petitioner and respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur in respect of the said fishery for the years 1396 BS to 1398 BS at a rent of Tk. 18,750.00. It appears from Annexure 'E' dated 6.9.89 that the petitioner Society is required to pay 10% higher rent for each successive year i.e. rent of Tk. 20,625.00 for the year 1397 BS and rent of Tk. 22,688.00 for year 1398 BS. On 12.8.89 by Annexure 'D' dated 12.8.89 the Tahsildar, Nilkhi Tahsil office delivered physical possession of the said fishery in favour of the petitioner society. Since the delivery of possession of the said fishery the petitioner society is in continuous possession uninterruptedly investing substantial amount of money in rearing and preserving fishes and for putting 'dal-kata, bamboo fencing, earth cutting, etc. On 22.8.89 respondent No. 5, Nikhil Chandra Malo, Secretary, Kabirajpur Union Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd., Upazila Rajair, District Madaripur out of grudge and enmity filed an application before the respondent No. 3, Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division), making allegations against the petitioner contending, inter alia, that the petitioner is not a fisherman but a cultivator; that the respondent No. 5, was previously possessing the said fishery for which respondent No. 5 could show no proof and that the respondent No. 5 came to know about the settlement of the said fishery in favour of the petitioner when a notification for auction was published on 30.3.90 for sale of the fisheries under Madaripur District excluding the disputed fishery and on enquiry came to know that on 12.2.89 the said fishery had already been settled with the petitioner by respondent No. 4, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur and that the respondent No. 5, was prepared to pay higher rent at the rate of 30% instead of 25% above the previous year's rent and to pay 15% instead of 10% higher rent for the remaining period of two years. The respondent No. 3, Additional Commissioner, Dhaka Division called for a report from the respondent, No. 4, in Appeal Case No. 65 of 1989. The respondent No. 4 Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur on 6.9.89 by his memo No. 2659 SA dated 6.9.89 (Annexure E) sent a report to the said respondent No. 3 stating that he had granted the settlement of the said fishery to the petitioner in accordance with the Ministry of Land's Memo No. 8-80/84-458(139) dated 15.10.89 (printed at pages 294-297) of the Land Administration Manual); that the District and Upazila Co-operative Officer as well as Chairman of the Local Upazila Parishad had duly certified that the petitioner is a duly registered co-operative society of genuine fishermen; that the respondent No. 5, Kabirajpur Union Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. had never taken lease of the fishery in question; that after expiry of the previous lease the fishery in question was put to auction for several times but no fishermen society came to participate in the auction, that the respondent No. 5 had filed an application to respondent No. 4 long after the execution of the lease deed Ext. C dated 21.3.89 and that the said application of respondent No. 5 was rejected by the respondent No. 4 on the ground that it was not fit for consideration. 

 3. It appears from order dated 22.11.89 (Annexure F) passed by respondent No. 3, Additional Commissioner, Dhaka Division that the petitioner had filed an application dated 15.2.88 to the respondent No. 1 Secretary, Ministry of Land praying for settling the fishery in question for 5 years in favour of his Nilkhi Arial Kha Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. upto 1399 BS and that the respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur by his memo No. 100-C dated 27.3.88 had forwarded the said application to the Ministry of Land and that the Ministry of Land also by its memo No. 655 dated 15.12.88 asked respondent No. 4 Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur for his opinion regarding settling the said fishery in favour of the petitioner on the basis of negotiated lease. The respondent No. 3, Additional Commissioner. Dhaka Division, by his order Annexure 'F' dated 22.11.89 set aside the duly executed lease (Annexure C) granted by respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur on 21.3.89 arbitrarily on the ground that the petitioner is a cultivator (although the petitioner is a registered Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity) and also on the ground that the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur had mentioned nothing about making of improvement of the Jalmahal by the petitioner and directed that the said Jalmahal should be put on auction. As the petitioner had taken delivery of possession of the fishery in question (Annexure D) on payment of initial payment of rent of Tk. 18,750.00 on 13.2.89 as per Duplicate Carbon Receipt (Annexure B) on the basis of "ঘরবাড়ী জলমহল ইজারা দলিল” and Annexure 'C' which was duly executed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur, respondent No. 4 on behalf of the President of Bangladesh, the order Annexure 'F dated 22.11.89 passed by the Additional Commissioner, Dhaka Division, respondent No. 3, arbitrarily cancelling the duly executed lease (Annexure-C) is illegal and without lawful authority as the respondent No. 3, Additional Divisional Commissioner had no authority to do so and also because the lease Annexure C dated 21.3.89 which was executed on behalf of the President of Bangladesh by a duly authorised officer, namely, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur does not contain any provision that it is subject to confirmation by the Commissioner/ Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division, or by any higher authority like the Land Appellate Board or the Secretary, Ministry of Land. Therefore, the order Annexure 'G' dated 27.2.90 passed by the Member-1, Land Appeal Board and the order Annexure-H dated 4.11.90 passed by Mr. AZM Nasiruddin, Secretary, Ministry of Land confirming the order dated 22.11.89 passed by the Additional Commissioner, respondent No. 3 are also illegal and without lawful authority. 

 5. On behalf of the respondent Nos. 1-4 an affidavit-in- opposition has been filed but it has nowhere been stated in the said affidavit that respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur had given settlement of the said fishery in favour of the petitioner Nilkhi Arial Kha Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. without obtaining approval of the Government and respondent No. 1, Secretary, Ministry of Land has not also upheld the order dated 22.11.89. (Annexure F) of the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division respondent No. 3, on that ground. So nowhere it was stated by any of the aforesaid Government officials that the lease in question granted in favour of the petitioner by respondent No. 4, is being cancelled because no approval was given by, the Ministry of Land. The respondent No: 5 in his affidavit-in-opposition has also not taken that ground and has not alleged that granting of lease by respondent No. 4 in favour of the petitioner is bad because no approval of the Ministry of Land was taken. The ground taken by respondent No. 5 is that the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur, respondent No. 4 acted illegally in granting lease in favour of the petitioner behind the back of the respondent No. 5. There is absolutely no reason why the respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) is required to hear respondent No. 5, Kabirajpur Union Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. before granting negotiated lease of the fishery in favour of the petitioner as the respondent No. 5 has no locus standi in such circumstances. On the grounds stated above, it is held that the lease of Shiruail to Nilkhi Baddha Jalmahal (closed fishery), Upazila Shibchar, District Madaripur dated 31.1.89 followed by respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur's order dated 6.9.89 (Annexure-E) for a period of three years from 1396 BS to 1398 BS executed in favour of petitioner Nilkhi Arial Kha Matsyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. by duly authorised respondent No. 4 the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur on behalf of the President of Bangladesh is a valid lease and that the order dated 22.11.89 (Annexure-F) passed by respondent No. 3, Additional Commissioner, Dhaka Division cancelling the said lease executed by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur in favour of the petitioner society, dated 27.2.90 (Annexure-G) passed by respondent No. 2, Member, Land Appeal Board, Dhaka and the order dated 4.11.90 (Annexure-H) passed by Respondent No. 1, Secretary Ministry of Land vacating the order of stay and thereby upholding the order dated 22.11.89 (Annexure-F) are illegal and without lawful authority. 

 6. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The order dated 22.11.89 (Annexure-F) and the Memo No. 683 (ম) (3) Appeal dated 18.12.89 (Annexure-F 1) passed by the Additional Commissioner, Dhaka Division (Respondent No. 3) and the order dated 27.2.90 in Appeal Case No. 2-52/89 (Jalmahal) (Madaripur) passed by Mr. Md. Monsurul Huq Khan, Member-1, Land Appeal Board, Dhaka upholding the aforesaid order dated 18.12.89 passed by the respondent No. 3, Additional Commissioner, Dhaka Division, Dhaka cancelling the deed of lease (Annexure-C) dated 21.3.89 granted in favour of the petitioner by respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur and Annexure-H being Memo No. Bhu:Ma; Sha:-26/90/1147 Appeal (signed by the respondent No. 1, Secretary, Ministry of Land on 4.11.90 and dispatched by the Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Land on 17.11.90 to the petitioner) upholding the cancellation of the aforesaid lease Annexure--'C' dated 21.3.89 passed by the respondent No. 3 are declared to be illegal, without lawful authority and of no legal effect. The lease deed Annexure-C dated 21.3.89 for the period from 1396 BS to the end of 1398 BS executed by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur clarified by Annexure-E dated 6.9.89 by the said Additional Deputy Commissioner(Revenue), Madaripur fixing annual rent at above 1396 BS's rent of Tk. 18,750.00 for the year 1397 BS. (See duplicate carbon receipt dated 17.12.90 Annexure-J) and further fixing annual rent for the year 1399 BS in respect of the said fishery at 10% higher than the annual rent for the year 1398 BS. 

 Let a copy of this order be sent to Respondent Nos. 1 and 4 immediately. Petitioner is directed to deposit the rent for the year 1399 BS within the month of Falgun, 1398 BS and Respondent No. 4 Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur is directed to collect the same from the petitioner preferably within the last day of Falgun, 1398 BS or at least within 8th Chaitra 1398 BS failing which he (Respondent No. 4) shall put, the fishery in question in public auction, on 1st or 2nd Baisakh, 1399 BS or within a week from 1st Baisakh, 1399 BS.
